identity.title: REsolved ALMA and SMA Observations of Nearby Stars (REASONS): A population of 74 resolved planetesimal belts at millimetre wavelengths

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present resolved dust observations of 74 planetary systems as part of the REsolved ALMA and SMA Observations of Nearby Stars (REASONS) survey and archival reanalysis.

targets.name: REASONS sample of 74 resolved planetesimal belts (e.g. GJ14, HD14055, HD191089)

evidence.quote: Distances are from *Gaia* DR3 (cite: Gaia2016b; Gaia2023j), or from *Hipparcos* if Gaia measurement not available (cite: vanLeeuwen2007).

distance_source.value: Gaia DR3, or Hipparcos if Gaia unavailable

evidence.quote: Distances are from *Gaia* DR3 (cite: Gaia2016b; Gaia2023j), or from *Hipparcos* if Gaia measurement not available (cite: vanLeeuwen2007).

question.value: What are the spatial properties (radius, width, vertical aspect ratio) and evolution of mm-resolved planetesimal belts across a uniformly modelled population of 74 systems?

evidence.quote: We uniformly modelled interferometric visibilities for the entire sample to obtain the basic spatial properties of each belt, and combined these with constraints from multi-wavelength photometry.
Fourteen targets were observed through project 2017.1.00200.S (PI: Matrà)
one (HD15745) through project 2017.1.00704.S (PI: Kral)

bands.value: Band 6 (1.27 mm) for new ALMA data

evidence.quote: All observations were carried out using Band 6 receivers.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Two 2 GHz windows at 243.1 and 245.1 GHz; two 1.875 GHz windows at 227.2 and 230.1 GHz covering CN and CO 2-1

evidence.quote: two 2 GHz-wide spectral windows centred at 243.1 and 245.1 GHz with a low spectral resolution (31.25 MHz)
The higher resolution spectral windows were set to cover the CN N=2-1 (J=5/2-3/2) and the CO J=2-1 transitions at 226.875 and 230.538 GHz, respectively.
The total bandwidth available for continuum was 7.75 GHz, with both polarisations combined.

arrays.value: 12-m array with 43-50 antennas; ACA for HD170773 and HD161868

evidence.quote: Data were taken using the 12-m array with 43-50 antennas in a single configuration per target, varying for different targets.

sensitivity.value: 12-68 uJy continuum for beams 0.2-3.1 arcsec (ALMA); 100-290 uJy for SMA

evidence.quote: Typical continuum sensitivities, measured in a region of the images that is free of emission, are 12-68 $\mu$Jy for beam sizes ranging between 0.2$\ensuremath{''}$ and 3.1$\ensuremath{''}$.

observing_dates.value: SMA between January 2018 and January 2019; ALMA Cycle 5

evidence.quote: between January 2018 and January 2019

provided.value: 10 new belts observed at 1.27 mm; calibrated archival SMA data

evidence.quote: 15 with ALMA (Sect. [3.1](#sec:almaobs)), and 10 with the SMA (Sect. [3.2](#sec:smaobs)).

provided.value: 850 um detections defining the flux-limited sample

evidence.quote: complete a resolved follow-up census of a flux-limited sample of sources detected at (sub-)mm wavelengths by the SCUBA-2 Observations of Nearby Stars (SONS) JCMT Legacy Survey (cite: Holland2017)

what.value: Protoplanetary ring widths (65 rings) from DSHARP, Taurus and ODISEA surveys

evidence.quote: We compile a sample of 65 protoplanetary rings from three ALMA surveys: DSHARP (cite: Huang2018), the Taurus star-forming region survey (cite: Long2018), and ODISEA

what.value: Archival ALMA, SMA, CARMA calibrated data of resolved belts

evidence.quote: For SMA and CARMA archival observations, we obtained calibrated, science-ready visibilities from PIs/co-Is of the respective projects

what.value: Stellar ages and memberships from BANYAN Sigma

evidence.quote: Membership from BANYAN Sigma (cite: Gagne2018), or moving group age also from (cite: Gagne2018)

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: L7 synthetic Kuiper belt model used to estimate Kuiper belt radius and width

evidence.quote: These values are estimated from the L7 synthetic model of the inner, main and outer Kuiper belt (cite: Kavelaars2009; Petit2011)

pipeline_or_manual.value: ALMA observatory pipeline; archival data calibrated with provided pipeline or scripts; SMA calibrated in MIR

evidence.quote: Standard calibrations were applied to each visibility dataset by the ALMA observatory, using its pipeline.
All concatenated datasets were imaged in the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA) software v5.4.0
The flux calibration accuracy of all ALMA observations was conservatively assumed to be 10%.
The continuum imaging was carried out in multi-frequency synthesis mode with multiscale deconvolution (cite: Cornwell2008).
Continuum imaging of the combined observations for each target was carried out using multiscale CLEAN deconvolution within CASA v5.4.0

weighting_robust.value: Different weighting and u-v tapers per target; natural weighting for CO

evidence.quote: Different weighting schemes and u-v tapers were used for different targets to find an optimal balance between surface brightness sensitivity and resolution.
CO imaging was carried out after continuum subtraction from the visibility measurements (using the uvcontsub CASA task).
We direct the reader to §3 of (cite: Matra2018b) for a full description of the requirements for a belt to be selected.

evidence.quote: following the method of (cite: Yelverton2019)

method.value: Pipeline calibration, concatenation, tclean multiscale imaging

evidence.quote: Standard calibrations were applied to each visibility dataset by the ALMA observatory, using its pipeline.

method.value: Radially and vertically Gaussian ring model from RADMC-3D images, Fourier transformed with GALARIO, fit with MCMC

evidence.quote: We then use the GALARIO software package (cite: Tazzari2018) to obtain a Fourier transform of the model image, and sample it at the same u-v locations as the data.

key_parameters.value: h fixed to 0.03 unless vertically constrained; temperature r^-0.5

evidence.quote: In other cases, we fix this value to $h=0.03$, motivated by the aspect ratio of the AU Mic disc (cite: Daley2019).

assumptions.value: Gaussian radial profile; large grains behave as blackbodies

evidence.quote: on the assumption that the large grains probed by millimetre observations are well approximated by blackbodies

fitting.value: Affine-invariant emcee v3, uniform priors, likelihood proportional to exp(-chi2/2), walkers = 10x free parameters, >=1000 steps, weight rescaling free

evidence.quote: We ran the MCMC to sample the posterior probability distribution of the parameters using a number of walkers equal to 10 times the number of free parameters

validation.value: Residual images and deprojected visibility profiles; 65/74 fit well

evidence.quote: Based on the compatibility of residual images with pure noise, we find that 65/74 belts are fit well by our radially and vertically Gaussian model.

method.value: Star + modified blackbody fit to multi-wavelength photometry

evidence.quote: fit it with a star + modified blackbody model, following the method of (cite: Yelverton2019)

analysis_steps.goal: Derive dust masses and test collisional evolution

method.value: Mass at 1.33 mm from flux, kappa and blackbody temperature; compare with collisional isochrones with age groups

evidence.quote: $\kappa_\nu$ is the dust opacity, assumed to be 0.23 m$^2$ kg$^{-1}$, by scaling down 1 m$^2$ kg$^{-1}$ at 1000 GHz linearly

key_parameters.value: t0 = 10 Myr, delta = 13/3, epsilon = 1, D ~2e-8 Myr Mearth au^-13/3

evidence.quote: We find that a good qualitative fit to the data can be found by setting $D\sim2\times10^{-8}$ Myr M$_{\oplus}$ au$^{-13/3}$.
Based on the compatibility of residual images with pure noise, we find that 65/74 belts are fit well by our radially and vertically Gaussian model.
we also test models with $\epsilon=0.4$

findings_qualitative.value: Most belts are broad rings, ~70% with fractional width >0.5, unlike protoplanetary rings

evidence.quote: roughly 70% of discs are wide ($\Delta R/R>0.5$)

claims.hypothesis: Belt masses deplete via radius-dependent collisional evolution
claims.experiment: Mass vs radius in three age groups with bias maps and isochrones
claims.result: ~2 dex mass depletion over ~2 dex collisional age; field belts follow R^13/3 locus
claims.finding: Consistent with t^-1 collisional depletion, faster for smaller belts

evidence.quote: provide strong evidence for (radius-dependent) collisional evolution of planetesimal belts

claims.hypothesis: Belts are narrow rings like protoplanetary rings
claims.experiment: Compare fractional widths of 50 belts with 65 protoplanetary rings
claims.finding: Belts are broad; unresolved substructure or migrating rings may explain

evidence.quote: A simple Kolmogorov-Smirnov test indicates a probability below $10^{-9}$

claims.hypothesis: Belt vertical heights increase with age via viscous stirring
claims.experiment: Aspect ratios of 24 belts vs age
claims.result: No trend with age; inclinations ~1-20 deg
claims.finding: Early stirring, inheritance, or diverse pathways

evidence.quote: we find no such trend in our data

why_this_method.value: Gaussian ring chosen as simple prescription to derive radius and width

evidence.quote: we deemed a Gaussian a simple enough prescription to derive the centroid radius $R$ and width (FWHM) $\Delta R$

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Slower epsilon=0.4 evolution overestimates old field belt masses

evidence.quote: significantly overestimates the mass of belts in the old field population

limitations_admitted.value: Sample biased by flux-density limits; heights may be extracted from azimuthal profile rather than resolved

evidence.quote: this does not necessarily mean that these belts were all vertically resolved

referee_caveats_inferred: Gaussian ring model biases widths for belts with substructure
Age uncertainties and 1.33 mm opacity assumption drive mass trends
Collisional isochrone comparison is qualitative, not fitted
